Core 2v2 machinery already exists; what remains is the scaled 4v4/6v6 version under the exact same heuristic allocator as the separated system. Allocator fixed, only parameter sharing changes.
RESEARCH_QUESTION: With CLOSEST_DEFENDS held byte-identical to the sealed separated 4v4 composite, does a single shared network pi_phi(a | o, z) that is forced to experience both strategy conditions still pass the joint crossover gate — or does parameter sharing erase specialization even when explicit strategy information z is provided?

separated_comparator_already_sealed.reading: physically separated strategy/role networks under heuristic allocation close 4v4

WHY_THIS_EXISTS.scientific_contrast: Fully shared pi_phi(a|o,z)  vs  Separated learned strategy networks, with the SAME CLOSEST_DEFENDS allocator in both. If separated PASSes and fully-shared forced-z FAILs, that is direct evidence that explicit strategy information alone is insufficient and parameter sharing itself is erasing specialization.
not_a_rediscovery_of: CLOSEST_DEFENDS (already sealed at 4v4 screen + used by DEFEND_ATTACK_SPLIT)
forced-z crossover / Delta_A / Delta_B / LCB95 / run_state.seal (already exist)

DEFEND_TEACHER_ROLE_CONDITIONING_A_V1 shared-network role bit without z (already failed; this arm adds explicit strategy z and evaluates forced-z crossover, not a retune of that failed teacher run)
WHY_THIS_EXISTS.not_the_failed_6v6_RUNG1: RUNG1_6V6 Share-Encoder crossover FAIL did not use CLOSEST_DEFENDS. This arm deliberately holds the allocator that made the separated 4v4 composite PASS, changing only the sharing architecture.

SINGLE_AXIS_locked.change_only: parameter sharing: one SharedActorCentralizedCritic plays every agent under every role and every forced strategy z. No second ATTACK/DEFEND network. No split_attack_defend splice.
held_fixed_vs_separated_PASS: CLOSEST_DEFENDS allocator (k = N/2 = 2 living agents closest to own_flag_home)
certified Pole A / Pole B overlays and config hashes
canonical Delta convention: Delta_A = V(z_A,A)-V(z_B,A), Delta_B = V(z_B,B)-V(z_A,B); PASS iff both means > 0 and both LCB95 > 0
matched-seed discipline across the 2x2 forced-z matrix
entity-repair warm-start base for the shared network (same pi_A checkpoint family as the separated ATTACK freeze)

ARCHITECTURE_locked.diagram: each episode: z ~ Uniform{z_A, z_B} (episode-static, forced — never inferred by a router); CLOSEST_DEFENDS(k=2) -> role bits r_i; every agent i executes the SAME network pi_phi(a_i | o_i, z, r_i)
ARCHITECTURE_locked.policy_form: pi_phi(a | o, z) with the CLOSEST_DEFENDS role bit r concatenated as the allocator interface (identical role channel the separated pi_D already uses). r is an INPUT, not a separate parameter set. There is exactly one Actor parameter tensor set for ATTACK and DEFEND and for both z.
ARCHITECTURE_locked.latent_actor_conditioning: concat (paper-faithful concat path; no FiLM, no per-z action heads, no private branches)
ARCHITECTURE_locked.router: ABSENT. No q_phi. No learned allocator. z is scheduled at training time and forced at evaluation time.
ARCHITECTURE_locked.no_hidden_separate_nets: Forbidden: loading a second SharedActorCentralizedCritic, splice_actions, frozen ATTACK copy, or any per-role module whose parameters are not shared with the single pi_phi.

warm_start.expansion: zero-init expand for role column AND for z embedding / critic z one-hot so t0 behavior matches native pi_A when z and r are neutralized under the existing warm-start contracts

ROLE_ALLOCATION_locked.rule: k living agents closest to own_flag_home at the first decision tick; roles held for the whole episode
ROLE_ALLOCATION_locked.identity_with_separated: byte-identical protocol to DEFEND_ATTACK_SPLIT_POLICY_A_V1 / CLOSEST_DEFENDS_SCREEN_4V4. This arm does not invent, retune, or learn an allocator.
ROLE_ALLOCATION_locked.why_role_bit_still_present: Without feeding r into pi_phi, CLOSEST_DEFENDS would not affect individual actions when both strategies use the same k=2. The allocator must remain causally live for the sharing-axis comparison; the change is that both roles share parameters rather than routing to separate networks.

TRAINING_locked.do_not_launch_on_this_pc_while: CLOSEST_SPLIT_LEARNED_DEFEND_6V6_V1 25k viability / collapse-watch is in flight. This SPEC freezes design only.
TRAINING_locked.z_schedule: episode-static Uniform{0,1}; both strategy conditions MUST appear in the training distribution so the shared net cannot collapse to a single unconditional policy
TRAINING_locked.opponent_matching: z_A episodes train against certified Pole A; z_B episodes train against certified Pole B. Matched so each forced mode sees its specialty opponent.
TRAINING_locked.note_on_teacher: Separated PASS used an N' DEFEND teacher on pi_D only. This sharing-axis first attempt deliberately sets defend_teacher_lambda=0 so the only architectural difference vs a naive shared role-conditioned net is the forced strategy z plus dual-pole matched training. Retuning a teacher on this arm is a separate PI decision, not this freeze.

CONTRACTS_before_any_seed_spend: C0 this SPEC status starts with FROZEN and is on disk before any train/eval seed is reserved for this arm

C1 z reaches the actor: LatentConditionedActor / SharedActorCentralizedCritic receives the scheduled or forced z_idx every forward; ablating z changes logits (max abs logit delta > 0 under a fixed obs batch)
C2 single parameter set: exactly one actor module; split_attack_defend_enabled=False; no second SharedActorCentralizedCritic loaded for ATTACK
C3 no hidden per-role networks: no per-z private action heads, no latent_population_birth_per_z_action_heads, no FiLM/deep-branch forks that instantiate separate ATTACK/DEFEND weights
C4 CLOSEST_DEFENDS identical to separated: same k=2, same closest-to-own_flag_home rule, role_fixed_for_episode=True; contract against the separated composite's allocator call path
C5 forced z at eval: fixed_latent_strategy_id honored; q_phi never sampled; eval path cannot choose z
C6 training sees both z: occupancy of z_A and z_B over a short rollout window each in (0.25, 0.75) under Uniform schedule
C7 pole matching: z_A episodes use Pole A opponent; z_B episodes use Pole B opponent

C8 same seeds/poles/metrics: exploratory and confirmatory blocks disjoint from training seed and from DEFEND_ATTACK_SPLIT blocks (216/217/218); certified pole hashes match confirmatory separated RESULT
